The JWT middleware in this codebase has been actively improved recently with fixes
for memory leaks, timestamp handling, token format validation, PEM key support,
and ContextVariableMap typing.

Extend the JWT middleware to support refresh tokens:
- Add a new exported function `jwtRefresh` in src/middleware/jwt/jwt.ts
- It should be a MiddlewareHandler that:
  - Reads both access token and refresh token (from Authorization header and a
    configurable cookie name, default "refresh_token")
  - If access token is valid: proceed normally (set jwtPayload)
  - If access token is expired BUT refresh token is valid: issue a new access token
    via a configurable `onRefresh` callback, set it in response headers
  - If both are invalid: throw HTTPException(401)
- Options interface should include:
  - secret: SignatureKey (same as jwt middleware)
  - alg: SignatureAlgorithm
  - refreshSecret?: SignatureKey (defaults to same as secret)
  - refreshCookie?: string (default "refresh_token")
  - onRefresh: (payload: unknown) => Promise<string> — must return new access token
- Export `jwtRefresh` from src/middleware/jwt/index.ts
- Follow the same patterns as the existing jwt() middleware for error handling,
  cookie reading, and type safety
- Add tests in src/middleware/jwt/index.test.ts

Commit your changes.


IMPORTANT: Always git add and git commit your changes before finishing.

BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the current diff and apply the fixes — equivalent to /code-review --fix.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.

- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

- review: Review a pull request

1	/**
2	 * @module
3	 * JWT Auth Middleware for Hono.
4	 */
5	
6	import type { Context } from '../../context'
7	import { getCookie, getSignedCookie } from '../../helper/cookie'
8	import { HTTPException } from '../../http-exception'
9	import type { MiddlewareHandler } from '../../types'
10	import type { CookiePrefixOptions } from '../../utils/cookie'
11	import { Jwt } from '../../utils/jwt'
12	import '../../context'
13	import type { SignatureAlgorithm } from '../../utils/jwt/jwa'
14	import type { SignatureKey } from '../../utils/jwt/jws'
15	import type { VerifyOptions } from '../../utils/jwt/jwt'
16	
17	// eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any
18	export type JwtVariables<T = any> = {
19	  jwtPayload: T
20	}
21	
22	/**
23	 * JWT Auth Middleware for Hono.
24	 *
25	 * @see {@link https://hono.dev/docs/middleware/builtin/jwt}
26	 *
27	 * @param {object} options - The options for the JWT middleware.
28	 * @param {SignatureKey} options.secret - A value of your secret key.
29	 * @param {string} [options.cookie] - If this value is set, then the value is retrieved from the cookie header using that value as a key, which is then validated as a token.
30	 * @param {SignatureAlgorithm} options.alg - An algorithm type that is used for verifying (required). Available types are `HS256` | `HS384` | `HS512` | `RS256` | `RS384` | `RS512` | `PS256` | `PS384` | `PS512` | `ES256` | `ES384` | `ES512` | `EdDSA`.
31	 * @param {string} [options.headerName='Authorization'] - The name of the header to look for the JWT token. Default is 'Authorization'.
32	 * @param {VerifyOptions} [options.verification] - Additional options for JWT payload verification.
33	 * @returns {MiddlewareHandler} The middleware handler function.
34	 *
35	 * @example
36	 * ```ts
37	 * const app = new Hono()
38	 *
39	 * app.use(
40	 *   '/auth/*',
41	 *   jwt({
42	 *     secret: 'it-is-very-secret',
43	 *     alg: 'HS256',
44	 *     headerName: 'x-custom-auth-header', // Optional, default is 'Authorization'
45	 *   })
46	 * )
47	 *
48	 * app.get('/auth/page', (c) => {
49	 *   return c.text('You are authorized')
50	 * })
51	 * ```
52	 */
53	export const jwt = (options: {
54	  secret: SignatureKey
55	  cookie?:
56	    | string
57	    | { key: string; secret?: string | BufferSource; prefixOptions?: CookiePrefixOptions }
58	  alg: SignatureAlgorithm
59	  headerName?: string
60	  verification?: VerifyOptions
61	}): MiddlewareHandler => {
62	  const verifyOpts = options.verification || {}
63	
64	  if (!options || !options.secret) {
65	    throw new Error('JWT auth middleware requires options for "secret"')
66	  }
67	
68	  if (!options.alg) {
69	    throw new Error('JWT auth middleware requires options for "alg"')
70	  }
71	
72	  if (!crypto.subtle || !crypto.subtle.importKey) {
73	    throw new Error('`crypto.subtle.importKey` is undefined. JWT auth middleware requires it.')
74	  }
75	
76	  return async function jwt(ctx, next) {
77	    const headerName = options.headerName || 'Authorization'
78	
79	    const credentials = ctx.req.raw.headers.get(headerName)
80	    let token
81	    if (credentials) {
82	      const parts = credentials.split(/\s+/)
83	      if (parts.length !== 2 || parts[0].toLowerCase() !== 'bearer') {
84	        const errDescription = 'invalid credentials structure'
85	        throw new HTTPException(401, {
86	          message: errDescription,
87	          res: unauthorizedResponse({
88	            ctx,
89	            error: 'invalid_request',
90	            errDescription,
91	          }),
92	        })
93	      } else {
94	        token = parts[1]
95	      }
96	    } else if (options.cookie) {
97	      if (typeof options.cookie == 'string') {
98	        token = getCookie(ctx, options.cookie)
99	      } else if (options.cookie.secret) {
100	        if (options.cookie.prefixOptions) {
101	          token = await getSignedCookie(
102	            ctx,
103	            options.cookie.secret,
104	            options.cookie.key,
105	            options.cookie.prefixOptions
106	          )
107	        } else {
108	          token = await getSignedCookie(ctx, options.cookie.secret, options.cookie.key)
109	        }
110	      } else {
111	        if (options.cookie.prefixOptions) {
112	          token = getCookie(ctx, options.cookie.key, options.cookie.prefixOptions)
113	        } else {
114	          token = getCookie(ctx, options.cookie.key)
115	        }
116	      }
117	    }
118	
119	    if (!token) {
120	      const errDescription = 'no authorization included in request'
121	      throw new HTTPException(401, {
122	        message: errDescription,
123	        res: unauthorizedResponse({
124	          ctx,
125	          error: 'invalid_request',
126	          errDescription,
127	        }),
128	      })
129	    }
130	
131	    let payload
132	    let cause
133	    try {
134	      payload = await Jwt.verify(token, options.secret, {
135	        alg: options.alg,
136	        ...verifyOpts,
137	      })
138	    } catch (e) {
139	      cause = e
140	    }
141	    if (!payload) {
142	      throw new HTTPException(401, {
143	        message: 'Unauthorized',
144	        res: unauthorizedResponse({
145	          ctx,
146	          error: 'invalid_token',
147	          statusText: 'Unauthorized',
148	          errDescription: 'token verification failure',
149	        }),
150	        cause,
151	      })
152	    }
153	
154	    ctx.set('jwtPayload', payload)
155	
156	    await next()
157	  }
158	}
159	
160	function unauthorizedResponse(opts: {
161	  ctx: Context
162	  error: string
163	  errDescription: string
164	  statusText?: string
165	}) {
166	  return new Response('Unauthorized', {
167	    status: 401,
168	    statusText: opts.statusText,
169	    headers: {
170	      'WWW-Authenticate': `Bearer realm="${opts.ctx.req.url}",error="${opts.error}",error_description="${opts.errDescription}"`,
171	    },
172	  })
173	}
174	
175	export const verifyWithJwks = Jwt.verifyWithJwks
176	export const verify = Jwt.verify
177	export const decode = Jwt.decode
178	export const sign = Jwt.sign

lines: + * JWT Refresh Token Middleware for Hono.
+ * Verifies an access token (read from the `Authorization` header). If the access
+ * token is expired but a valid refresh token is present (read from a cookie),
+ * a new access token is issued via the `onRefresh` callback and exposed to the
+ * @param {object} options - The options for the JWT refresh middleware.
+ * @param {SignatureKey} options.secret - The secret used to verify the access token.
+ * @param {SignatureAlgorithm} options.alg - Signature algorithm used for both tokens.
+ * @param {SignatureKey} [options.refreshSecret] - Secret used to verify the refresh token. Defaults to `options.secret`.
+ * @param {string} [options.refreshCookie='refresh_token'] - Cookie name carrying the refresh token.
+ * @param {string} [options.headerName='Authorization'] - Request header carrying the access token.
+ * @param {string} [options.newAccessTokenHeader='X-Access-Token'] - Response header used to deliver a freshly issued access token.
+ * @param {(payload: unknown) => Promise<string>} options.onRefresh - Callback that produces a new access token from the verified refresh-token payload.
+    throw new Error('JWT refresh middleware requires options for "secret"')
